sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Origin**: Started in 1914 by **Jatra Bhagat** in the Gumla district of Jharkhand (then Bihar). 
• **Ideological Core**: A blend of **Sanskritization** (adopting vegetarianism, teetotalism, and sacred threads) and **Anti-Colonialism** (refusal to pay land taxes or work as coolies for landlords/British).
• **Religious Shift**: Moved away from traditional Oraon animism toward a **monotheistic** belief system, emphasizing the worship of 'Dharmesh' (Supreme God).
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The movement acted as a bridge between tribal identity and the **Non-Cooperation Movement (NCM)**, with Tana Bhagats becoming staunch followers of Mahatma Gandhi.

sections.title: Comprehensive Classification & Comparative Matrix
rows: Oraon tribe, Chota Nagpur; focus on purity and moral reform.
Reaction against Christian missionary influence and traditional tribal superstitions.
Prelims: Understanding the 'Sanskritization' process in tribal societies.
Alignment with INC; refusal of taxes; participation in 1920-21 NCM.
Influence of Gandhian ideology; demand for 'Swaraj' and land rights.
Mains: Tribal integration into the national freedom struggle.

items.definition: Derived from the Oraon word meaning 'to pull' or 'to drag', symbolizing the act of pulling out the evil spirits and colonial exploitation.
A term used for the followers who adopted a life of devotion, asceticism, and moral discipline.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Gandhian Alignment**: Tana Bhagats were the only tribal group to adopt the spinning wheel (Charkha) and Khadi as a symbol of resistance.
• **Legislative Impact**: Their persistent struggle contributed to the strengthening of the **Chota Nagpur Tenancy (CNT) Act** protections.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Severe repression by British authorities, confiscation of land, and imprisonment of leaders.
• **Solutions**: Post-independence, the Tana Bhagat Development Authority was established to preserve their unique cultural identity and socio-economic upliftment.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: **J-O-G** (Jatra, Oraon, Gandhi).
• **Decoded Meaning**: **J**atra Bhagat (Leader) + **O**raon (Tribe) + **G**andhi (Ideological alignment).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses Tana Bhagat with Munda Ulgulan. Remember: Munda Ulgulan (Birsa Munda) was earlier (1899) and more militant, whereas Tana Bhagat (1914) was more Gandhian and reformist.
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Subaltern Nationalism' to describe how tribal movements like Tana Bhagat reinterpreted Gandhian Swaraj through their own cultural lens.

keyTakeaways: The Tana Bhagat movement represents the evolution of tribal resistance from isolationist to nationalist.
It is a classic case study of 'Sanskritization' as a tool for social mobilization.
The movement's adherence to non-violence (Ahimsa) made it unique among contemporary tribal uprisings.
